title: Themes
text:
theme() takes a preset and individual options. The presets follow ggplot2’s complete themes:







Preset
Look




vega
Vega-Lite’s defaults


gray (also grey, ggplot2)
gray panel with white grid lines, and ggplot2’s hue palette


bw
white panel with a dark border and light grid


linedraw
white panel with a black border and thin black grid lines


minimal
light grid, no border, and no axis lines


classic
axis lines and no grid


light
light gray border and grid


dark
dark background


void
no axes or grid



baseSize: scales every font size, with ggplot2’s proportions. Themes are written into the specification as Vega-Lite config, so HTML and static exports look the same.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->theme('gray', baseSize: 12);

The individual options are:

font, textColor, and baseSize
legendPosition (right, left, top, bottom, or none), legendDirection (horizontal or vertical), and legendTitle: false
background, panelBackground, and panelBorder
grid, gridColor, axisLine, and ticks
xLabelAngle and yLabelAngle, which turn axis labels anticlockwise as element_text(angle =) does
titleAnchor and padding

config: accepts raw Vega-Lite config, merged last. Calls without a preset build on the current theme.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->theme('minimal', legendPosition: 'bottom', font: 'Georgia, serif', config: ['axis' => ['labelColor' => '#666666']])
    ->labs(title: 'A minimal theme with the legend below');

A page can also choose a theme at render time. The vega-embed option theme accepts the vega-themes names, and phiz adds 'auto', which follows the reader’s light or dark mode preference:
$plot->embed(['theme' => 'auto']);

title: Scales, coordinates, and labels
text:
scaleX(), scaleY(), scaleColor(), scaleFill(), scaleSize(), scaleShape(), scaleOpacity(), and scaleLinetype() configure the scale and guide for one aesthetic. Successive calls for the same aesthetic merge.
Scale options are passed to the Vega-Lite scale:

type: linear, log, sqrt, pow, symlog, time, ordinal, quantile, quantize, or threshold
domain and range
scheme, a Vega color scheme such as viridis, blues, set2, or tableau10
values, a manual palette as a level-to-value map or a list in level order
zero, nice, reverse, clamp, base, exponent, domainMid, and padding

Guide options are passed to the axis or legend:

name, the title
breaks, the tick or legend values
format, a d3 number or time format
labels, a label formatter (below), a map from values to labels, a list of labels for breaks, or a Vega label expression
guide: false, which hides the axis or legend

use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::economics())
    ->aes(x: 'pop', y: 'pce')
    ->point(alpha: 0.4)
    ->scaleY(type: 'log', breaks: [500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000], name: 'Personal consumption ($bn, log scale)')
    ->scaleX(format: '.3s', name: 'Population (thousands)');

use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(size: 40)
    ->scaleColor(values: ['f' => '#1B9E77', 'r' => '#7570B3', '4' => '#D95F02'], name: 'Drive');

Continuous position scales fit the data as in ggplot2: points and lines do not force the axis to include zero. Plots with bars, areas, histograms, or densities keep zero, since their lengths are measured from it. zero: true restores Vega-Lite’s default for a single scale.
The functions in Phiz\ include ggplot2’s shortcuts. Each returns a closure for the pipe operator or apply():







Function
Scale




scale_x_log10(), scale_x_sqrt(), scale_x_reverse(), scale_x_date()
transformed and date position scales


scale_x_discrete(limits:, labels:)
discrete positions: limits orders and subsets the levels, labels renames them


scale_color_manual(values)
a level-to-color map, or colors in level order


scale_color_brewer(palette), scale_color_distiller(), scale_color_fermenter()
ColorBrewer palettes for discrete, continuous, and binned data


scale_color_viridis_d(), _c(), _b()
viridis with option (A magma to E cividis, H turbo), begin, end, and direction


scale_color_gradient(), scale_color_gradient2(), scale_color_gradientn()
two-color, diverging, and many-color gradients


scale_color_hue(h:, c:, l:, hStart:, direction:)
ggplot2’s hue palette with its options


scale_color_grey(start:, end:)
grays, as grey.colors()


scale_color_identity()
the data values are the colors, with no legend



Each scale_color_*() has a scale_fill_*() twin. The hue and grey palettes are computed for the number of levels in the data.


The label functions follow the scales package. Pass one as labels:.



Function
0.256
12500




label_percent()
25.6%
1250000%


label_comma()
0.256
12,500


label_dollar()
$0.256
$12,500


label_number(accuracy: 0.1, suffix: ' kg')
0.3 kg
12,500.0 kg


label_scientific()
2.56e-1
1.25e+4


label_date('%b %Y')
for dates




accuracy rounds (0.01 keeps two decimals, and the default trims trailing zeros), scale multiplies first, and prefix and suffix wrap the number. label_dollar(scale: 0.001, suffix: 'k') writes 12500 as $12.5k.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\guide_axis;
use function Phiz\label_percent;
use function Phiz\scale_fill_viridis_d;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'class', fill: 'drv')
    ->bar(position: 'fill')
    ->scaleY(labels: label_percent(), name: 'Share of cars')
    ->apply(scale_fill_viridis_d(begin: 0.2, end: 0.8))
    ->guides(x: guide_axis(angle: 45))
    ->labs(x: null, fill: 'Drive');




guides() sets the axis or legend for each aesthetic, as ggplot2’s guides() does. 'none' hides one. guide_axis(angle:) turns axis labels, guide_legend(title:, ncol:, direction:) arranges a legend, and guide_colorbar(barwidth:, barheight:) sizes a color bar. Any other Vega-Lite axis or legend property can be passed as a named argument.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\scale_color_grey;
use function Phiz\scale_x_discrete;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'drv', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->boxplot()
    ->apply(scale_x_discrete(limits: ['f', 'r', '4'], labels: ['f' => 'Front', 'r' => 'Rear', '4' => '4WD']))
    ->apply(scale_color_grey())
    ->guides(color: 'none')
    ->labs(x: 'Drive', y: 'Highway mpg')
    ->theme('bw');

title: Laravel and Livewire
text: phiz’s Laravel service provider is discovered automatically. It registers the <x-phiz> Blade component and the @phizScripts directive. Without Laravel, the same classes are never loaded.

title: Laravel and Livewire
text:
Blade
<x-phiz :plot="$plot" class="h-80" />
The component accepts a Plot, a Compose, a specification array, or specification JSON. :options passes vega-embed options, merged over config('phiz.embed_options'). Other attributes go to the container element.
The first <x-phiz> on a page adds the script tags. To place them yourself, put @phizScripts in the layout.

title: phiz
text:
phiz builds Vega-Lite specifications from PHP with a grammar modeled on ggplot2. Vega-Lite handles the layout, scales, interaction, and rendering. PHP code describes the plot, and you write no JavaScript. The same specification renders in the browser through vega-embed, or to SVG, PNG, or PDF through the vl-convert binary for reports and email.
Every chart on this site was produced by running the code shown above it. The examples live in docs/examples/, and scripts/docs-examples.php runs them and embeds the specifications they returned.

title: phiz
text:
Install
composer config repositories.phiz vcs https://github.com/phpstats/phiz
composer require phpstats/phiz:dev-main
phiz requires PHP 8.5 and has no other dependencies. Static export needs the vl-convert binary. Laravel support is optional and is discovered automatically.

title: phiz
text:
What phiz covers

A fluent, immutable Plot builder, and ggplot2-style functions for PHP’s pipe operator.
About 30 geoms, including points, lines, areas, bars, histograms, densities, boxplots, intervals, reference lines, text, heatmaps, smoothers, QQ plots, and arcs.
Scales, coordinate flips and limits, facets, compositions, labels, and themes modeled on ggplot2’s complete themes.
Tooltips, pan and zoom, brushing, legend highlighting, sliders, and linked views, all expressed as Vega-Lite parameters.
Statistical plots built from php-stats model results and CmdStanPHP draws: coefficient plots, regression diagnostics, predicted values with confidence bands, and posterior intervals.
HTML output, static export, and an <x-phiz> Blade component that re-renders inside Livewire.

title: phiz
text:
The phpstats family
phiz is the visualization package of the phpstats family. php-stats fits the models, phibble provides data frames, phplyr provides dplyr verbs, and CmdStanPHP runs Stan. phiz depends on none of them. It reads any of their tables directly.

title: Get started
Get started
Get started
Get started
Get started
text:
Output
A plot compiles to a Vega-Lite specification on demand.
$plot->toArray();        // the specification as a PHP array
$plot->toJson();         // as JSON
$plot->embed();          // an HTML fragment with the container and script tags
$plot->html();           // a standalone HTML page
$plot->svg();            // SVG through vl-convert
$plot->save('plot.pdf'); // the file extension picks the format
Rendering covers the options for each output, and Laravel and Livewire covers the Blade component.

title: Facets and composition
Facets and composition
Facets and composition
Design
text:
phiz does not draw graphics. It translates a ggplot2-style description into a Vega-Lite specification. Vega-Lite then resolves scales, lays out facets and legends, runs transforms, handles interaction, and renders to canvas or SVG. The PHP side stays small, and plots behave the same in the browser and in static export.
Most statistics run where Vega-Lite runs them: bins, densities, loess fits, aggregates, quantiles, and window functions are Vega-Lite transforms. phiz computes a statistic in PHP only when Vega-Lite cannot:

the confidence bands of smooth() with lm, quad, or poly
curve() evaluations of PHP functions
the bandwidth behind density(adjust:)
the statistics helpers’ intervals and predictions

title: Design
text:
Differences from ggplot2
Coming from ggplot2 lists the translations and the behaviors that differ.

title: Design
text:
Versions
phiz emits Vega-Lite 6 specifications. The pinned browser libraries are vega 6.4.0, vega-lite 6.4.3, and vega-embed 7.3.0. Static export uses vl-convert with Vega-Lite 6.1, and the tests validate every specification against the Vega-Lite 6.1.0 JSON schema, the version both renderers support.

title: Dashboards with Livewire
text: This page builds a small dashboard of linked charts. A Livewire component holds the filters, phplyr summarizes a phibble table on the server, and phiz renders three charts that all follow the same state. Changing a filter re-renders the component, and each chart re-embeds in place.

title: Dashboards with Livewire
Dashboards with Livewire
Dashboards with Livewire
Dashboards with Livewire
text:
Choosing where to compute
The two approaches suit different data:

Server-side summaries send only the summarized rows to the page. They suit large tables, database queries, and statistics that need PHP, such as model fits. Each interaction costs a Livewire round trip.
Browser-side linking sends the raw rows once and responds to every interaction immediately. It suits up to a few thousand rows. Large data covers what to do beyond that.

Both approaches can share a page. For example, a Livewire filter can choose the rows, and a brush can explore them in the browser.

title: Plan: CmdStanPHP figures on phiz
text: This page proposes how CmdStanPHP’s figures can use phiz. It is written as an issue for CmdStanPHP and changes nothing there. It builds on CmdStanPHP’s planning note, docs/notes/phiz-readiness.md. Whether and when to proceed is the CmdStanPHP maintainer’s decision.

title: Plan: CmdStanPHP figures on phiz
text:
Background
CmdStan\Plot computes each figure’s statistics in PHP and returns a CmdStan\Figure: a kind, a title, data rows, and metadata. Figure renders the rows as ASCII text, as a Vega-Lite 5 spec, as an HTML page, and as SVG or PNG through vl-convert. The R comparisons check the data rows, so they stay valid as long as the rows do not change.
phiz now provides what the readiness note lists as prerequisites:







Prerequisite
phiz




Inline, precomputed data with identity stats
every geom accepts rows; col(), line(), point(), and rule() draw values as given


Bars with explicit bin edges
col(aes(xmin: 'x0', xmax: 'x1', y: 'count'))


Rules at constant values
hline(), vline(), and mapped yintercept


Points with conditional color
a nominal color mapping with a fixed domain and range


Row facets with shared y scales and header labels
facetGrid(rows: 'chain', labeller: 'both') or header: ['labelExpr' => ...]


Spec, JSON, HTML, SVG, and PNG with pinned versions
toArray(), toJson(), html(), svg(), png(); vega 6.4.0, vega-lite 6.4.3, vega-embed 7.3.0, vl-convert with Vega-Lite 6.1

title: Plan: CmdStanPHP figures on phiz
text:
Proposed steps

Optional Figure::toPhiz(). Add a method that returns a Phiz\Chart when phiz is installed, and throws a clear error otherwise. Detect phiz with class_exists(\Phiz\Plot::class), as to_frame() detects phibble. Keep vegaLite(), html(), svg(), and png() unchanged for PHP 8.2 users.
Tests. For each figure kind, assert that toPhiz() produces a spec that validates against the Vega-Lite schema and renders with vl-convert. Compare its data values with Figure::$data. Exact spec equality with VegaLite::spec() is not a goal, because phiz targets Vega-Lite 6 and applies its own defaults.
Move shared rendering. When CmdStanPHP requires PHP 8.5, replace Figure::html() and the vl-convert code in Figure::convert() with phiz’s Html and Export. The binary discovery already honors the VL_CONVERT variable.
Rebuild the kinds. Replace VegaLite::spec() with the toPhiz() translations and keep the Figure data contract and the R comparisons.

title: Plan: CmdStanPHP figures on phiz
text:
Translations
Each kind maps to a short phiz plot over the existing Figure::$data rows. These translations were compiled and rendered with vl-convert, using rows shaped like each kind’s data.
use Phiz\Plot;
use function Phiz\{aes, factor};

$rows = $figure->data;
$m = $figure->meta;

$plot = match ($figure->kind) {
    'trace' => Plot::of($rows)
        ->aes(x: 'iteration', y: 'value', color: factor('chain'))
        ->line(linewidth: 0.8, alpha: 0.8)
        ->labs(y: $m['variable'], color: 'chain'),

    'hist' => Plot::of($rows)
        ->col(aes(xmin: 'x0', xmax: 'x1', y: 'count'))
        ->labs(x: $m['variable']),

    'dens' => Plot::of($rows)
        ->aes(x: 'x', y: 'density', color: $m['by_chain'] ? factor('chain') : null)
        ->line(linewidth: 1.5)
        ->labs(x: $m['variable']),

    'intervals' => Plot::of($rows)
        ->aes(y: \Phiz\field('variable', 'nominal', sort: array_column($rows, 'variable')))
        ->rule(aes(x: 'll', xend: 'hh'), linewidth: 1.5)
        ->rule(aes(x: 'l', xend: 'h'), linewidth: 5)
        ->point(aes(x: 'm'), size: 70, fill: '#FFFFFF', stroke: '#000000')
        ->labs(x: 'value', y: null),

    'rank_hist' => Plot::of($rows)
        ->col(aes(xmin: 'x0', xmax: 'x1', y: 'count'))
        ->hline(aes: aes(yintercept: 'mean(expected)'), linetype: 'dashed')
        ->facetGrid(rows: 'chain', labeller: 'both')
        ->labs(x: 'rank', y: 'count'),

    'scatter' => Plot::of($rows)
        ->aes(x: 'x', y: 'y', color: 'divergent:N')
        ->point(alpha: 0.4)
        ->scaleColor(domain: [false, true], range: ['#4C78A8', '#D62728'], guide: false)
        ->labs(x: $m['x_variable'], y: $m['y_variable']),

    'acf' => Plot::of($rows)
        ->aes(x: 'lag:O', y: 'acf')
        ->col()
        ->hline(0)
        ->facetGrid(rows: 'chain', labeller: 'both')
        ->labs(y: 'autocorrelation'),

    'pareto_k' => Plot::of($rows)
        ->aes(x: 'observation', y: 'k')
        ->hline($m['threshold'], linetype: 'dashed', color: 'gray')
        ->hline(1, color: '#D62728')
        ->point()
        ->labs(y: 'Pareto k'),
};

return $plot->title($figure->title);
The intervals kind uses the same column names (ll, l, m, h, hh) as phiz’s interval_plot(), which computes the rows itself from draws_columns() output. A CmdStanPHP user can call interval_plot($fit->draws_columns()) directly.

title: Plan: CmdStanPHP figures on phiz
text:
Open questions

PHP floor. phiz requires PHP 8.5. Until CmdStanPHP raises its floor from 8.2, phiz stays an optional dependency, and steps 3 and 4 wait.
Thinning. VegaLite::thin() keeps every k-th draw and every divergent draw. It belongs in CmdStanPHP as a row filter applied before toPhiz().
ASCII output. phiz has no text backend. AsciiChart stays in CmdStanPHP.

title: Data and fields
text:
Plot::of() and each geom’s data: argument accept data in several shapes:

a list of row arrays, such as [['x' => 1, 'y' => 2], ...]
an array of equal-length columns, such as ['x' => [1, 2], 'y' => [2, 3]]
a phibble table, or any object with toRows() or toColumns()
a Laravel Collection, or any object with toArray()
any iterable of rows, where rows may be arrays or objects
Data::url('cars.csv'), which Vega-Lite fetches in the browser
Data::named('live'), a data source the page supplies at runtime

Inline data is embedded in the specification. Values are made safe for JSON: DateTimeInterface values become ISO 8601 strings, enums become their values, and NAN and INF become null, which Vega-Lite treats as missing.
use Phiz\Plot;

$columns = [
    'month' => ['2026-01-01', '2026-02-01', '2026-03-01', '2026-04-01', '2026-05-01', '2026-06-01'],
    'visits' => [1200, 1350, 1290, 1610, 1820, 1765],
];

$plot = Plot::of($columns)
    ->aes(x: 'month', y: 'visits')
    ->line()
    ->point(size: 50);

title: Data and fields
text:
Field types
Vega-Lite needs a measurement type for every mapped field. phiz infers it from inline data:

quantitative, when every non-null value is an integer or a float
temporal, when every value is an ISO date or date-time string
nominal, otherwise

A numeric code such as a cylinder count is quantitative by this rule. It gets a continuous color scale and gradient legend unless you mark it as categorical. Field shorthand sets the type explicitly with a suffix: :Q (quantitative), :N (nominal), :O (ordinal), or :T (temporal). factor('cyl') is the equivalent of R’s factor(cyl), and its levels: argument sets the order.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\factor;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mtcars())
    ->aes(x: 'wt', y: 'mpg', color: factor('cyl'), shape: 'am:N')
    ->point(size: 60)
    ->labs(color: 'Cylinders', shape: 'Manual');

URL data cannot be inspected in PHP, so phiz assumes quantitative positions and nominal groupings. Use shorthand types for anything else.

title: Data and fields
Data and fields
Data and fields
text:
Field definitions
field() builds a Field with any Vega-Lite field-definition property, such as field('date', timeUnit: 'month', title: 'Month') or field('term', sort: ['b', 'a', 'c']). A raw array is also accepted for any aesthetic and is used as given.
Field names containing dots or brackets, such as R’s Sepal.Length, are escaped automatically. Vega-Lite would otherwise read them as nested access.

title: Development
text:
composer test
The suite runs with Pest and covers several layers:

Spec snapshots for every geom, feature, statistics helper, and gallery example, in tests/.pest/snapshots/. After an intended change, run vendor/bin/pest --update-snapshots and review the diff.

When vl-convert is available, a render of every gallery example to SVG. Some specifications pass the schema but fail to compile, and this smoke test catches them.

Tests that need the php_stats extension skip when it is not loaded. The saved fits in tests/fixtures/fits.json cover the rest.

Gallery

title: Development
text:
Documentation
The documentation is a Quarto website in docs/. The pages include generated fragments for their examples:

Each file in docs/examples/ returns a chart.
php scripts/docs-examples.php runs every example. For each one it writes the code and the resulting specification to docs/_generated/, and an SVG to docs/figures/. It also copies the gallery.
quarto render docs builds the site into docs/_site/.

title: Geoms
text:
Each geom adds a layer. Every geom method accepts these common arguments:
As in ggplot2, color is the outline of bars, areas, and tiles, and fill is their interior. For points, lines, and text, color is the main color. linetype accepts ggplot2’s names (dashed, dotted, dotdash, longdash, twodash), hex dash strings such as '44', or a dash array.

title: Geoms
Geoms

text:
Intervals
errorbar(), linerange(), and pointrange() draw intervals from ymin to ymax. With xmin and xmax they are horizontal. position: 'dodge' places groups side by side, which the coefficient plots use to compare models.
use Phiz\Plot;

$estimates = [
    ['site' => 'North', 'mean' => 4.1, 'lower' => 3.2, 'upper' => 5.0],
    ['site' => 'East', 'mean' => 5.3, 'lower' => 4.6, 'upper' => 6.1],
    ['site' => 'South', 'mean' => 3.4, 'lower' => 2.1, 'upper' => 4.6],
    ['site' => 'West', 'mean' => 4.8, 'lower' => 4.2, 'upper' => 5.5],
];

$plot = Plot::of($estimates)
    ->aes(x: 'site', y: 'mean', ymin: 'lower', ymax: 'upper')
    ->errorbar(width: 10)
    ->point(size: 60)
    ->hline(4.5, linetype: 'dashed', color: '#888888')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Mean score (95% CI)');

title: Geoms
text:
Reference lines
hline() and vline() draw rules at fixed values, at every value of a list, or at a mapped yintercept or xintercept field. abline() draws y = intercept + slope * x across the range of the data.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')
    ->point(alpha: 0.4)
    ->abline(0, 1, linetype: 'dashed')
    ->hline(30, color: '#D62728')
    ->vline(20, color: '#1F77B4')
    ->labs(x: 'City mpg', y: 'Highway mpg');

title: Geoms
Geoms
Geoms
Geoms
Geoms
text:
Annotations
annotate() adds a layer from fixed values rather than data, as ggplot2’s annotate() does. It draws text, label, point, segment, rect, rule, pointrange, linerange, errorbar, or crossbar. Positions can be single values or lists, and -INF and INF reach the edges of the panel. Annotations ignore the plot’s mappings, keep its axis titles, and appear in every facet panel.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')
    ->annotate('rect', xmin: 15, xmax: 20, ymin: -INF, ymax: INF, fill: 'orange', alpha: 0.2)
    ->count(alpha: 0.6)
    ->annotate('segment', x: 30, y: 25, xend: 33.5, yend: 42.5, color: '#D62728')
    ->annotate('text', x: 30, y: 23, label: 'Most efficient', color: '#D62728')
    ->labs(x: 'City mpg', y: 'Highway mpg');

title: Geoms
text:
Raw layers
layer() adds any Vega-Lite layer as given, and geom() adds a geom by name with explicit parameter and style arrays.

title: Coming from ggplot2
text: phiz follows ggplot2’s grammar: data, aesthetic mappings, layers of geoms, scales, coordinates, facets, labels, and themes. Most ggplot2 code translates line by line. This page lists the translations, then the places where phiz behaves differently because Vega-Lite renders the plot.

title: Coming from ggplot2
text:
Translating a plot
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  facet_wrap(~year) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Displacement (L)", y = "Highway mpg") +
  theme_minimal()
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(alpha: 0.5)
    ->smooth(method: 'lm')
    ->facetWrap('year')
    ->scaleY(type: 'log')
    ->labs(x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg')
    ->theme('minimal');
The pipe form is closer still:
ggplot($mpg, aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv'))
    |> geom_point(alpha: 0.5)
    |> geom_smooth(method: 'lm')
    |> facet_wrap('year')
    |> scale_y_log10()
    |> labs(x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg')
    |> theme_minimal();
Aesthetics are named arguments, so aes(displ, hwy) becomes aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy'). Field names are strings. colour and alpha are accepted as aliases of color and opacity.

title: Coming from ggplot2
text:
Differences
These differences follow from Vega-Lite rendering the plot.

Sizes. Point size is an area in square pixels, as in Vega-Lite, rather than a diameter in millimeters. The default is 30. linewidth is in pixels.
Bins. bins: is a maximum, and Vega-Lite rounds the boundaries. Use binwidth: and boundary: for exact bins.
Limits. xlim() and ylim() zoom without removing data. ggplot2 removes the data outside the limits, which changes statistics computed from it.
Densities. The default bandwidth is Vega-Lite’s. adjust: multiplies R’s bw.nrd0, so adjust: 1 reproduces ggplot2’s default.
Smoothers. Loess, lm, quad, and poly fits and their confidence bands are computed in PHP and match R. Loess matches loess(surface = "direct"); ggplot2 interpolates the loess surface, which moves the curve slightly. Above 3,000 rows, loess falls back to Vega-Lite’s transform without a band, where ggplot2 switches to a GAM. There is no gam method.
Colors. Categorical colors come from Vega-Lite’s palette by default. theme('gray') switches to ggplot2’s hue_pal() colors, computed for the number of levels. scaleColor(values:) or scheme: sets them explicitly.
Panels. A discrete axis is 300 pixels by default, the same as a continuous axis, and grows by 20 pixels per level beyond 15 levels.
Violins. violin() draws each violin as a Vega-Lite trail, whose ends are rounded. There is no draw_quantiles option; layer a boxplot() instead.
Polar coordinates. coordPolar() draws bars, columns, and arcs. Vega-Lite has no polar form for lines, points, or areas, so radar charts are not available.
Not available. There is no sec_axis(), no geom_dotplot(), and no geom_quantile(). Use raw() or layer() for any Vega-Lite feature phiz does not wrap.

title: Coming from ggplot2
text:
Additions
phiz adds features that ggplot2 leaves to other packages:

tooltips, pan and zoom, brushing, legend highlighting, and sliders (see Interaction)
linked views across compositions
the statistics helpers for php-stats fits and CmdStanPHP draws (see Statistics)
Vega-Lite aggregates and time units in field shorthand, such as 'mean(hwy)' and 'year(date):O'

title: Interaction
text: Interaction in phiz is expressed as Vega-Lite parameters, so it works in any page that renders the specification. Static exports draw the initial state.

title: Interaction
Interaction
Interaction
Interaction
Large data
text: phiz embeds inline data in the specification, and the browser keeps every row in memory to draw it. A few thousand rows render immediately. Hundreds of thousands of rows make the page heavy and slow, so large data should be summarized before it is sent. phiz does that summarizing in PHP.

title: Large data
text:
Sizes to expect







Rows embedded
Effect




up to about 5,000
renders immediately, and interaction stays smooth


5,000 to 20,000
renders, but brushing and tooltips slow down


above 20,000
phiz raises a warning; the page grows by several megabytes


millions
summarize in PHP or in the database



Config::$warnRows sets the warning threshold (20,000 by default, or null to turn it off). In Laravel it is config('phiz.warn_rows'). The warning is an E_USER_WARNING that names the alternatives below.

title: Large data
Large data
text:
Tables stay columnar
A phibble table or an array of columns is kept as given. The binning geoms read it column by column, and rows are built only if the specification embeds them. On a laptop, a million-row phibble Frame plots as follows:



Plot

title: Large data
Large data
Large data
text:
Other approaches

Summarize first. A phplyr group_by() |> summarise() or a SQL GROUP BY usually answers the question with far fewer rows. Dashboards with Livewire shows charts built from summaries.
Load from a URL. Data::url('/data/points.csv') lets the browser fetch the file, so the page itself stays small. The browser still holds every row, so this helps page size, not drawing speed.
Sample. Bin::sample() keeps a uniform random subset when a scatterplot of individual points matters more than exact counts.

title: Rendering
text:
toArray() returns the Vega-Lite specification and toJson() encodes it. Plots also implement JsonSerializable. The specification declares the Vega-Lite 6 schema.
Four escape hatches reach the parts of Vega-Lite that phiz does not wrap:

raw([...]) deep-merges arbitrary Vega-Lite into the top level. Nested objects merge, and lists and scalars replace.
transform(...) adds Vega-Lite transforms that run before every layer.
layer([...]) adds a raw Vega-Lite layer.
param() and select() add raw parameters.

text:

Four escape hatches reach the parts of Vega-Lite that phiz does not wrap:

raw([...]) deep-merges arbitrary Vega-Lite into the top level. Nested objects merge, and lists and scalars replace.
transform(...) adds Vega-Lite transforms that run before every layer.
layer([...]) adds a raw Vega-Lite layer.

title: Rendering
text:
HTML
embed() returns a container element followed by the script tags, and html() returns a standalone page. Both pass vega-embed options, such as ['actions' => false] or ['renderer' => 'svg'].
The container carries the specification in a data-phiz attribute. A small loader script, about 100 lines, renders every such element with vega-embed. It renders them again when the attribute changes. The same markup therefore works in static pages, Blade views, and Livewire components.
The browser libraries are pinned:



Library
Version




vega
6.4.0


vega-lite
6.4.3


vega-embed
7.3.0



Assets chooses where they come from:
use Phiz\Assets;

$plot->embed(assets: Assets::cdn());                 // jsDelivr, with subresource integrity (the default)
$plot->embed(assets: Assets::local('/js/vega'));     // copies you serve: vega.min.js, vega-lite.min.js, vega-embed.min.js
$plot->html(assets: Assets::inline('/path/to/js'));  // embedded in the page, for offline files
$plot->embed(assets: Assets::none());                // your bundle already sets window.vegaEmbed
$plot->embed(assets: false);                         // just the container

title: Rendering
Statistics
text:
The statistics helpers build ordinary plots from model results, so their output can be restyled with any Plot method. They read the arrays that php-stats returns. Formula fits from stats_lm, stats_glm, stats_lmer, and stats_glmer name their coefficients in columns. Matrix fits from stats_ols and stats_logistic take a names: argument.
The fits on this page were produced by php-stats from the mtcars data and saved in docs/examples/fits/.
